title: Smokehouses, salting and curing
h1: Smokehouses, salting and curing: what the craft was, what science explained later, and why there is no formula here
dek: Monticello and Mount Vernon record who salted and smoked the meat, and where it went. Later science explained part of why it kept. This page gives no formula and says why.
description: What Monticello, Mount Vernon and Navy records show about salting and smoking meat, what science later explained, and why no historical method is a safe home guide.
recheck: If any listed source changes, when the Mount Vernon encyclopedia and the farm records behind both museum pages are read directly, or if USDA or NCHFP revise their curing and smoking guidance.

safety_review.scope: Gated (curing/smoking, botulism). Items for the human reviewer: (1) the page contains no cure formula, ratio, brine strength, time or curing temperature; (2) it cites USDA's hot-smoking page only to say that it concerns cooking, not smoke-curing, and does not reproduce its temperature range; (3) the verdict is not-validated; (4) it rests on the register's verified FSIS and NCHFP entries as summarized there (not re-read this session) plus the NCHFP history overview, the FSIS smoking page and the FSIS mold guide (dated 2013).
